value.introduction: Catherine Kent is an OHSU pediatrician whose profile lists general pediatric care, including medication management for depression, anxiety and ADHD.
value.story: Kent grew up in Portland and studied community health alongside American studies. Her OHSU biography traces her interest in pediatrics to that background and a summer counseling children and teenagers with serious illnesses. She trained at OHSU and returned after six years at Kaiser Permanente. Away from work, she describes coaching soccer, baking, running and playing futsal.

helpsWith: Medication management for depression, anxiety and ADHD
approach: Supporting children and families through childhood and adolescence

value.introduction: Stacy Drasen is an OHSU pediatrician whose profile lists well-child visits, illness care, autism evaluations and inpatient newborn care.
value.story: Drasen describes a path from Wisconsin to pediatric training in San Francisco, practice in the Bay Area, and work at The Vancouver Clinic before joining OHSU in early 2025. Her biography presents teaching as a new challenge alongside continued learning. She emphasizes listening and clear communication in her own account of care. Outside work, she mentions reading, cooking, plants, pets and time outdoors.

approach: Listening and clear communication, as described by the clinician

value.introduction: Erika Meyer is a pediatrician listed at Metropolitan Pediatrics’ NW Portland clinic, with a professional interest in child development.
value.story: Before medicine, Meyer taught elementary school and studied cultural anthropology. Her practice biography describes subsequent medical study at Harvard and pediatric residency at OHSU. In her own account of care, she considers children within their family context. The same biography names reading, travel and outdoor activities among her interests.

approach: Considering children within their family context, as described by the clinician
